extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors of observational epidemiology studies (epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, journal editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reviewing reports of observational epidemiologic research (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) so that all essential items are clearly and transparently reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE checklist (22 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: A checklist of 22 items considered essential for good reporting of observational studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 22 items cover title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and other information; they are intended as guidance on what to report to enable assessment of strengths, weaknesses and generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract (item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1 of the STROBE checklist pertains to what should be reported in the title and abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure title and abstract present key information about the study to allow readers to understand study design and main findings at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction (items 2 and 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items 2 and 3 relate to the Introduction section of a report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report background/rationale and specific objectives or hypotheses so readers understand the study's context and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods (items 4–12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items 4 through 12 cover the Methods section of an observational study report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the methodological details (study design, participants, variables, data sources/measurement, bias, study size, quantitative variables, statistical methods, etc.) sufficiently to allow assessment and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results (items 13–17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items 13 through 17 concern the reporting of study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present participants, descriptive data, outcome data, main results, and other analyses clearly and transparently so readers can evaluate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion (items 18–21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items 18 through 21 address the Discussion section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss key results, limitations, interpretation, and generalisability in a way that acknowledges strengths and weaknesses and places findings in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information (item 22: funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 22 covers other information, explicitly funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sources of funding and the role of funders to allow assessment of potential conflicts of interest or influences on the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design coverage: cohort, case-control, cross-sectional
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE recommendations cover three main analytical designs: cohort studies, case-control studies, and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the checklist items relevant to the specific design used and report design-specific details as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-specific items (items 6, 12, 14, 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four checklist items (6, 12, 14, 15) are design-specific rather than common to all designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the appropriate wording and requirements for these items depending on whether the study is cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of scope: reporting guidance, not quality appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE is a reporting guideline focused on what is reported rather than a tool to evaluate quality of conduct or study design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the checklist as a substitute for methodological quality appraisal; use it to assess completeness and transparency of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of extensions for specific contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Several extensions (e.g., STROBE-ME, RECORD, STROBE-MR, STROBE-Vet) address reporting for specific areas or data types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, use the relevant STROBE extension (molecular epidemiology, routinely collected health data, Mendelian randomization, veterinary studies, etc.) to ensure domain-specific reporting items are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use of STROBE
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can use STROBE to check whether all essential items have been adequately reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist as a tool to assess completeness of reporting during peer review, but complement it with methodological appraisal where appropriate.
